title: Day 01 - prototype 01
note: The purpose of creating the prototype is to develop a simple concept demo. At the bottom of the screen, rockets move upward, while players control the mouse. Bullets are fired to shoot down the rockets.

title: Day 02 - Prototype 02
note: The space lunchbox moves from the top of the screen to the bottom. Players control the mouse to shoot down the lunchboxes. After consecutively hitting two lunchboxes, missiles randomly fire at the rockets to take them down. This version features a prototype of the spaceship, represented by a green triangle to symbolize the player's ship.

title: Day 03 - Build foundation scene (Can't see the background image?)
note: When adding a new background image, I found that the artifact in Claude Desktop could not display it. The error messages provided some help for debugging, but after several attempts, the background image still failed to show correctly. Eventually, I accidentally downloaded the file and opened it in Google Chrome, only to discover that the background image displayed normally.

title: Day 04 - Collaborate with AI and embark on a journey
Day 05 - Build Super Weapon
image: 05 Special weapon rocket clearing mechanic - Claude.png
note: During the game testing, I noticed that when there were too many rockets on the screen, not all of them could be cleared. Eventually, I decided to create a special weapon, similar to an aurora cannon effect, to eliminate all the rockets on the screen. Throughout this process, the AI presented its ideas in a storyboard format, making our communication feel truly interactive.
During the process, I requested the AI to create a conceptual prototype for me to understand the entire operation and its effects.
The Code architecture analysis helps us better understand the current structure of the source code, making the process of code integration smoother for me in the future.
